source.title: On the Varied Faces of Overparameterization in Supervised and Self-Supervised Learning
source.authors: Matteo Gamba; Arna Ghosh; K. Krishna; Agrawal; Blake A. Richards; Hossein Azizpour; Mårten Björkman

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests how width relates to test error using width sweeps in ResNet18s and ConvNets, rather than the one-hidden-layer ReLU networks in V2.
record.gate_note: The paper reports width-dependent supervised test-error curves and SSL linear-probe test-error trends. It does not test fixed random-label fitting, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, or example removal. Figure values are not stated numerically in the text.
record.test_reason: The supervised width sweeps test V2 in new convolutional architecture settings: test error improves again beyond interpolation. The method remains a width sweep with train/test evaluation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the conclusion: supervised and non-contrastive SSL pipelines show different width-dependent feature geometry, and no double descent is observed for SSL in the tested range. The authors report an inverse relation between spectral decay and input sensitivity, although Table 1 shows weak correlations in some supervised CIFAR-100 settings. The SSL absence claim is empirical, not theoretical.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fixed-depth convolutional networks, width sweeps, and feature-geometry measures; does not reproduce the one-hidden-layer ReLU experiment in V2.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed width trend differs between supervised learning and self-supervised objectives; SSL results are reported for Barlow Twins and BYOL.

fits_no_version.finding: SSL linear-probe performance improves with encoder width without observable double descent over the tested range, but no interpolation threshold is established.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider ResNet18 encoders improve downstream linear-probe performance under the tested Barlow Twins and BYOL recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral decay and feature input-Jacobian norm are negatively correlated; correlations are strong for SSL but weaker for some supervised settings, reaching -0.05 for ResNet18 on CIFAR-100 with 20% noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature spectral decay inversely tracks input sensitivity, with strength depending on architecture, dataset, and objective.

fits_no_version.finding: Frozen SSL features permit recovery of up to 60% of corrupted labels with 80% label noise; the supervised baseline fits corrupted targets beyond base width 9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frozen SSL representations can preserve label-denoising ability where end-to-end supervised models memorize corrupted targets.

record.problems: Relevant width-curve values are reported in figures without numerical values in the text; the paper describes trends but does not report uncertainty for these results. The experiments use convolutional architectures and do not match V2's stated one-hidden-layer network setup.

untested.parts: No matched demonstration of near-perfect fitting of fully random labels and natural-label generalization by the same architecture and recipe; partial label corruption does not establish this comparison.

The original one-hidden-layer networks and datasets are not reproduced. Supervised networks receive 1000 epochs rather than a demonstrated convergence criterion; exact threshold widths and error magnitudes are not recoverable from the supplied text. SSL results do not establish the required zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No controlled optimizer comparison; supervised and SSL pipelines change objectives and other recipe components alongside optimizer.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison against norm and margin measures.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence.

record.verdict_notes: The SSL findings do not justify a limits_scope verdict for V2: monotonic improvement does not contradict it, and the required interpolation threshold is unestablished. Differences between supervised and SSL results cannot be attributed solely to objective: optimizer, batch normalization, training duration, and weight decay also differ. Appendix A.3 reports three random seeds, although the supplied text does not quantify uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: No fixed random-label fit versus natural-label generalization comparison.

Uses convolutional ResNet18 and ConvNet families on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, not one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10; reports width trends but not exact interpolation-threshold widths or test-error values.
No fully connected versus convolutional comparison.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Measures feature Jacobian norm and spectral-decay coefficient, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: ResNet18 encoder with Barlow Twins linear probe
rows.stage_stated: self-supervised pretraining followed by linear-probe evaluation
rows.operation_detail: Varied encoder base width and measured linear-probe test error.
rows.note: The text reports no observable double descent for the displayed SSL settings and says increasing width monotonically improves train and test loss.
rows.check: Linear-probe test-error improvement does not establish improvement beyond a width that achieves zero training error. Absence of double descent is not a limitation of V2, which does not require an interpolation peak.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature Jacobian spectral norm across widths and label-noise settings.
rows.measure: Feature Jacobian spectral norm; described as mirroring the test-error double descent.
rows.note: This is a measured property related to the gap, but it is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
rows.check: Input sensitivity of features is neither V2's test error nor V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness.

rows.subject: ResNet18

rows.subject: Supervised ConvNet and ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Computed Spearman rank correlation between spectral-decay coefficient α and feature Jacobian norm.
rows.measure: Spearman rank correlation ρ between α and input Jacobian norm
rows.note: Values are listed in the table under the CIFAR-10 supervised setting, in the order 0%, 10%, 20% label noise.
rows.check: The reported CIFAR-10 correlations are correct but do not measure a listed version. Separate architecture and noise conditions. Table 1 also reports substantially weaker correlations for ResNet18 on CIFAR-100.

rows.note: The paper describes a strong anti-correlation; values are reported by objective and dataset.
rows.check: The reported correlations are correct but do not measure a listed version. Separate objective and dataset conditions.
